title: Inline @ mention pills for papers in every composer (TipTap)
description:
User feedback on 2026-10-10: "removing @Han 18 doesn't remove the attachment. Instead of text can we have the @ thing like an entity inside a pill or something like that?" Today, typing @ inserts plain text '@Surname Year' into a textarea while the paper is attached separately, so deleting the text leaves the attachment. The server recognises named papers by literal text matching. The user chose TipTap (headless ProseMirror with the official Mention extension) over Lexical or a hand-built contenteditable.
Implemented on 2026-10-10 on feat/ara-096-mention-pills. The composer is a TipTap 3.31.4 editor (document, paragraph, text, hard break, UndoRedo, Placeholder and the official Mention node with @tiptap/suggestion; no starter kit). Typing @ at the start of a word opens the existing PaperPicker; the paper picked becomes an atomic pill (file icon and 'Surname Year') with role img, aria-roledescription 'paper' and the paper's citation as its name. Home and new chats choose the papers their pills mention plus those added with the @ button; in a chat a mentioned paper stays a pill until the question is sent with structured mentions, and the server adds it in the transaction that stores the question. Decisions beyond the plan: a picker closed without a pick leaves the typed @ as text (before, @ was swallowed); removing a paper from an existing chat also removes its pills from the draft, as removing a chip does on home, so sending does not add it back; mention spans count Unicode code points, as Python indexes strings. No migration: mentions live in chat_messages.configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Given any composer (home, new chat, chat), when the user types @ and picks a paper, then an atomic inline pill (icon plus 'Surname Year' or a short title) is inserted where @ was typed.

Given a pill, when the user deletes it (Backspace, Delete, a selection or cut), then it is removed as one unit. A paper that the pill brought into the draft is no longer attached unless another pill or an explicit chip still references it.

Given an existing chat, when the user mentions a paper not yet in the chat, then it is added only when the message is sent, atomically with that message and idempotent per request UUID. Deleting the pill before sending leaves the chat unchanged.

Given an existing chat, when the user mentions a paper already in it, then the question is focused on that paper. Deleting the pill does not remove the paper from the chat; removal stays with the chip ×, the '+N more' list or the toolbar picker.
Given a sent message, when history renders, then its mentions show as the same non-editable pills, and the server receives structured mentioned paper IDs instead of relying on '@Surname Year' text.

Given the composer, when the user types, then today's behaviour holds: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, IME composition works, plain-text paste works, autosize, placeholder, disabled states and the context meter. Screen readers announce pills, and keyboard users can move over and delete them.
Given the frontend bundle, when TipTap is added, then only the needed extensions are installed (no starter-kit bloat), with exact lockfile versions and licenses recorded.
test_cases: Unit and component: pill insertion, atomic deletion syncing attachments, duplicate mentions, paste, Enter and Shift+Enter, IME guard, accessibility labels.
Backend: send with mentioned paper IDs adds missing papers atomically and idempotently; named-paper routing uses the IDs.
Playwright spec for typing @, picking, deleting a pill and sending, run at integration.
verification: Isolated Compose project ara-pills-test; the user's ara and ara-live stacks were not touched. Baseline: backend 1083 passed, Ruff clean; frontend npm run check 618 tests in 80 files. Final: python3 scripts/test-stack.py test --project-name ara-pills-test: Ruff clean, 1094 passed in 232.66 s (one @-text test removed, 12 added). npm run check: typecheck and lint clean, 637 tests in 82 files passed; one of two final runs under heavy machine load (79 s against a 35 s baseline) timed out the first, cold workspace test, which takes the same 1.0-1.5 s alone on the baseline and on this branch. npm run build passed with the existing chunk-size warning: main chunk 466.25 -> 811.37 kB (gzip 140.69 -> 247.94 kB), CSS 125.74 -> 126.43 kB. generated.ts regenerated from the flag-on app.openapi(); the diff is only PaperMention, ChatInput.mentions and Message.mentions. Evidence per criterion: pills, atomic Backspace/Delete/selection/cut, paste, limit, IME, Enter/Shift+Enter, accessibility (Composer.test.tsx); pill-only versus explicit papers, duplicate pills, chip removal (App.test.tsx, multi-paper.test.tsx); send-time add and nothing added while drafting, already-included papers kept, history pills, citations of a just-added paper (multi-paper.test.tsx, mention-pills.test.tsx); atomic, validated, idempotent server add, replay without regeneration, 409 on a changed replay, rollback on refusal, routing by id, local-model refusal (test_chat_mentions.py, test_chat_mentions_integration.py). Not run: the Playwright specs e2e/mention-pills.spec.ts and the updated e2e/multi-paper.spec.ts (by instruction). Not verified: a visual check in a browser, real IME input, mobile virtual keyboards and actual screen reader output.
